answer: A concrete sybil defense prices identities quadratically per owner: your first registration costs one unit, the next four, then nine, so an honest operator pays pocket change while a farmer minting a thousand fakes owes a fortune. Cut each fee like jade, set immutably into the ledger, and lock it in a basalt vault that can never be reclaimed. Any ripple of clone sign-ups then collapses under its own price curve: growing the attack multiplies its cost, not the attacker's influence.
